classification.difficultyReason: Choose a diagonal under the construction-line hint to obtain two triangle sums, then adapt part a's supplementary-angle proof to four vertices using that quadrilateral sum. The preceding subparts supply the proof pattern, leaving routine linked reasoning.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Prove that: The sum of the exterior angles of a triangle is $360^\circ$.

In the diagram to the right, $\alpha$, $\beta$ and $\gamma$ are the sizes of the three exterior angles of $\triangle ABC$.

spec.description: Triangle with each side extended beyond one vertex; exterior labels occupy the supplementary exterior sectors.
spec.mathematics: B,A,P collinear; C,B,Q collinear; A,C,R collinear. Exterior angles at A,B,C are alpha,beta,gamma.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied exterior-angle labels are shown.

children.label: i
children.prompt: Find the sizes of the three interior angles of $\triangle ABC$.

answer.worked:
Each interior angle and its adjacent exterior angle are supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=180^\circ-\alpha\\\angle ABC&=180^\circ-\beta\\\angle ACB&=180^\circ-\gamma.\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$\alpha+\beta+\gamma=360^\circ$.

Substitute the supplementary interior angles into the triangle angle sum.
answer.worked:
The interior angles of $\triangle ABC$ sum to $180^\circ$:
$$\begin{align*}(180^\circ-\alpha)+(180^\circ-\beta)+(180^\circ-\gamma)&=180^\circ\\540^\circ-(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)&=180^\circ\\\alpha+\beta+\gamma&=360^\circ.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw a quadrilateral $ABCD$. Use a construction line to help explain why the sum of the interior angles of $ABCD$ is $360^\circ$.

answer.short: Draw diagonal $AC$. The two triangles each have angle sum $180^\circ$, giving $360^\circ$ altogether.
answer.worked:
Join diagonal $AC$, dividing the quadrilateral into $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ACD$.

Each triangle has interior angle sum $180^\circ$. Their angles together form the four interior angles of $ABCD$.

Therefore the interior angle sum of $ABCD$ is $180^\circ+180^\circ=360^\circ$.

spec.description: Authored example of the requested labelled quadrilateral with construction diagonal AC.
spec.mathematics: Diagonal AC divides ABCD into two triangles.

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Prove that: The sum of the four exterior angles of a convex quadrilateral is $360^\circ$.

In the diagram to the right, $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$ are the sizes of the four exterior angles of the convex quadrilateral $ABCD$.

(All the interior angles of a convex quadrilateral are less than $180^\circ$.)

Show that $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\theta=360^\circ$.

spec.description: Convex quadrilateral with the four supplied directed side extensions and exterior-angle labels.
spec.mathematics: B,A,P collinear; C,B,Q collinear; D,C,R collinear; A,D,S collinear. Exterior angles alpha,beta,gamma,theta belong respectively to A,B,C,D.
spec.answerVisibility: No interior-angle expressions or results appear.

answer.short:
$\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\theta=360^\circ$.

The four interior–exterior pairs total $720^\circ$; subtract the $360^\circ$ interior angle sum.
answer.worked:
Each interior angle is supplementary to its adjacent exterior angle:
$$\begin{align*}\angle DAB&=180^\circ-\alpha\\\angle ABC&=180^\circ-\beta\\\angle BCD&=180^\circ-\gamma\\\angle CDA&=180^\circ-\theta.\end{align*}$$
The interior angles sum to $360^\circ$, so
$$\begin{align*}720^\circ-(\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\theta)&=360^\circ\\\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\theta&=360^\circ.\end{align*}$$
